SplashClean %1$s. Free and open source (GPL-3.0). No ads, no analytics, no account; nothing on your screen leaves the phone.

Built on: GKD selector engine and rule format (GPL-3.0, gkd-kit/gkd) · PaddleOCR PP-OCRv4 models (Apache-2.0) · ONNX Runtime (MIT) · libadb-android (GPL-3.0-or-later / Apache-2.0) · Conscrypt, Bouncy Castle.

After this one-time step the app can switch its accessibility service back on by itself (after a reboot, a cleaner, or a system hiccup) and skips the \"restricted setting\" prompt. The permission survives reboots and app updates; it is removed only when you uninstall the app.
Turn on USB debugging, connect the phone and run:

Xiaomi / Redmi: also turn on \"USB debugging (Security settings)\" (needs a SIM card and a Mi account).\nOPPO / OnePlus / realme: turn on \"Disable permission monitoring\" in Developer options.\nAll phones: Developer options are unlocked by tapping \"Build number\" 7 times in About phone.
Android 10 and older cannot pair wirelessly; use the computer method.

1. Tap Start: Developer options open.
2. Turn on Wireless debugging (connect to any Wi-Fi first); tick "Always allow on this network" and tap Allow.
3. Tap "Pair device with pairing code" and keep that dialog open.
4. Pull down the notification shade and type the 6-digit code into SplashClean's notification (tap its arrow if the "Enter code" button is hidden).

• Lock SplashClean in the recent-apps screen (pull down on its card or tap the lock icon).\n• Do not \"force stop\" it or clear it with a cleaner app: a force stop makes Android turn the accessibility service off. With the one-time authorization it comes back the next time the app runs.\n• If skipping stops, open SplashClean once.

Android 13+ blocks accessibility for apps installed from a file. Try to turn the service on once (the warning appears), then open App info → ⋮ (top right) → Allow restricted settings, and turn it on again. The one-time authorization removes this step.

Settings → Apps → Manage apps → SplashClean:
• Autostart: on
• Battery saver: No restrictions
• Other permissions: allow "Display pop-up windows while running in the background"
Then lock the app in Recents.

Settings → Apps → App launch → SplashClean: turn off \"Manage automatically\", then allow Auto-launch, Secondary launch and Run in background.\nSettings → Battery → More battery settings: \"Stay connected when device is asleep\".\nThen lock the app in Recents.
Settings → Apps → App management → SplashClean → Battery usage: allow background activity, auto launch and launch by other apps.\nThen lock the app in Recents.

Settings → Battery → Background power consumption management → SplashClean: allow high background power consumption.\ni Manager → App manager → Permission manager → Autostart: on.\nThen lock the app in Recents.
Settings → Battery → Background usage limits → Never sleeping apps: add SplashClean.\nSettings → Apps → SplashClean → Battery: Unrestricted.

Stops apps from downloading ads from third-party ad networks (Pangle, GDT, Baidu, Kuaishou, Sigmob…). Only DNS lookups go through it; nothing leaves the phone. It cannot block the in-house ads of big apps (Taobao, JD, Zhihu, Bilibili…) — skipping still handles those. It uses the phone\'s single VPN slot: it cannot run together with another VPN or proxy app.
Private DNS is set to a specific server, which bypasses this filter. Set Private DNS to Off or Automatic.

Some splash ads open another app or a shop page when the phone moves. For the apps you pick, SplashClean switches off the motion sensors, so shaking does nothing there. Side effect: those apps also lose their own shake, step or compass features (screen rotation keeps working). Needs the one-time authorization; after a reboot it is re-applied automatically the next time the phone is on Wi-Fi.
Pick apps that show \"shake / twist / tilt\" ads. Changes apply when you go back.
